key_insight: Variational quantum algorithms can approximately prepare and identify the low-energy Laughlin manifold of the ν=1/3 fractional quantum Hall state on near-term hardware.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how particle-number-preserving VQE/VQD workflows can be adapted to benchmark quantum processors on strongly correlated topological matter beyond simple toy models.
method: Formulated the lowest-Landau-level fractional quantum Hall problem in second quantization for the V1 Haldane pseudopotential.
Used particle-number-preserving variational circuits with VQE for ground states and VQD for excited-state reconstruction.
Benchmarked two geometries: Haldane sphere for a unique Laughlin ground state and torus for the threefold topological ground-state degeneracy.
evidence_signal: The authors compared variational results to exact diagonalization using energy estimates, error-mitigated observables, and subspace-containment diagnostics.
watch_item: The demonstrations are limited to small system sizes, so scalability and noise sensitivity on larger, more realistic quantum Hall problems remain open concerns.
paper_title: Toward Quantum Utility in Correlated Topological Matter: Variational Preparation of Fractional Quantum Hall Manifolds
